title: MapReduce
tagline: Break the job into 'map' and 'reduce' steps, and let the cluster run them in parallel.
what_it_is: MapReduce is a programming model for processing large datasets in parallel across a cluster, structured around two steps: 'Map,' which processes and transforms each piece of data independently, and 'Reduce,' which aggregates the mapped results into a final output.
key_points: Map step: applies a function to every piece of input data independently and in parallel, producing key-value pairs.
Shuffle step: groups all values with the same key together across the cluster, preparing them for reduction.
Reduce step: aggregates all values for each key into a final result (e.g. sum, count, average).
Designed so each step can run on a different machine, processing its slice of data without needing to see the whole dataset.
Largely replaced by Apache Spark in modern pipelines because Spark keeps data in memory and is much faster for iterative jobs.
why_it_exists: Writing custom distributed code to coordinate many machines, handle failures, and combine results is extremely hard to get right. MapReduce exists to give developers a simple, standardized two-step pattern (map, then reduce) so they can write distributed jobs without manually handling cluster coordination themselves.
intuition: To count how many times each word appears across a warehouse full of books, hand each worker a stack of books (Map: each worker tallies words in their own stack independently). Then, have workers combine their tallies by word — everyone with 'the' tallies hands their numbers to one person to sum (Reduce: aggregate by key). No worker ever needs to see the whole warehouse at once.

steps.title: Split input
steps.description: The large dataset is split into chunks distributed across the cluster.

steps.title: Map
steps.description: Each chunk is processed independently and in parallel, producing intermediate key-value pairs.

steps.title: Shuffle and sort
steps.description: All values sharing the same key are grouped together across the cluster, regardless of which machine produced them.

steps.title: Reduce
steps.description: Each group of values for a key is aggregated into a final output value, e.g. a total count or sum.

when_to_use: Understand MapReduce as the conceptual foundation for distributed batch processing, even if you use Spark in practice.
Use the actual MapReduce framework only in legacy Hadoop environments where Spark isn't available.
when_not_to_use: Do not choose raw MapReduce for new projects — Spark performs the same kind of processing significantly faster by keeping data in memory.
Do not use MapReduce for iterative algorithms (like many machine learning training loops) — its disk-based model between steps makes repeated passes slow.
common_mistakes: Underestimating how much slower MapReduce is compared to Spark for jobs that need multiple passes over the same data.
Writing overly complex chains of MapReduce jobs when a single Spark job could express the same logic much more simply.
ds_usage: Rarely written directly anymore in new pipelines, but understanding it is essential context for why Spark exists and how distributed batch processing conceptually works under the hood.
